audit.whatIsWrong: Steadfast Presence's dash-stop is attributed to the passive — "Steadfast Presence W passively cancels your E Elastic Slingshot dash and grounds you", and elsewhere "a passive-armor stance that stops your E dash dead".
audit.why: Riot's text splits the ability cleanly: "Poppy passively gains Armor and Magic Resist... Poppy can ACTIVATE Steadfast Presence to gain Move Speed and stop enemy dashes around her. If a dash is stopped, the enemy is slowed and grounded." The passive half is only resistances. The dash-stop is on the active, which is the entire reason baiting it works — and the entry's own mid-game section correctly says to bait it, directly contradicting its own early-game section. A player who believes the cancel is passive will conclude the matchup is unplayable and never look for the window.
audit.corrected: The dash-stop is the ACTIVE. The passive is armour and magic resist only.

audit.whatIsWrong: Steadfast Presence is named as the ability that decides the lane in six separate places and never given a cooldown once.
audit.why: It is 20/18/16/14/12s. At rank 1 that is a twenty-second window after she spends it — comfortably long enough for Zac to reset E (21/18/15/12/9s), walk up and run a full pattern. That single number turns the entry's repeated 'bait her W' instruction from a slogan into a plan, and its absence is why the matchup reads as hopeless.
audit.corrected: Steadfast Presence 20s at rank 1; Heroic Charge 14s; Keeper's Verdict 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Keeper's Verdict is treated purely as a counter-engage that cancels Zac's R; nothing says what Poppy is doing while she casts it.
audit.why: Keeper's Verdict is a channel and Poppy is untargetable during it. That is why trying to burst her out of the channel fails and why the answer is spacing rather than damage. It is also 140/120/100s, so an ultimate she spends on a bad angle is two full minutes of free engages.
audit.corrected: Keeper's Verdict is a 140s channel and she is untargetable during it.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says "Poppy's level 1 Steadfast Presence W cancels your only engage tool" as the reason she wins level 1.
audit.why: Zac has no Elastic Slingshot at level 1, so there is nothing for W to cancel — and Poppy taking W first is not the normal level-1 pick either. Level 1 is lost to Hammer Shock and Heroic Charge simply out-damaging an ability-poor Zac, which is a different lesson.
audit.corrected: Her Q and E out-trade you before your slingshot exists.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's tracked ability and focus for this matchup is Heroic Charge.
audit.why: Every bespoke sentence in the content layer correctly identifies Steadfast Presence as the ability that decides the lane, and the kits agree — it is the only ability in either champion's kit that answers Zac's engage outright. Heroic Charge is a wall-conditional stun on 14s. The full layer is tracking the second-most important cooldown.
audit.corrected: Track Steadfast Presence; Heroic Charge is secondary.

notes: All five packet suspectNames for this matchup are FALSE POSITIVES. 'Let's Bounce' is already "Let's Bounce!" on disk (the detector strips the exclamation mark). 'Bait Steadfast Presence', 'Hold Steadfast Presence', 'Save Keeper's Verdict' and 'Her Hammer Shock' were all matched at edit distance 4-5 against the correct names — the detector is counting the leading verb or pronoun ('Bait ', 'Hold ', 'Save ', 'Her ') as part of the ability name. That pattern accounts for most of the suspectName noise across the whole Zac packet and is worth fixing in the detector: strip a leading word before measuring distance. The one genuine error here was mechanical, not nominal — the dash-stop was attributed to Steadfast Presence's passive when it is on the active. Poppy's derived kit flags also carry two grounding false positives (Hammer Shock and Keeper's Verdict); only Steadfast Presence actually grounds, and only when it stops a dash. I wrote nothing that relies on the other two. UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Keeper's Verdict genuinely cancels Zac's R mid-flight. The existing text asserts it in three places and a large displacement plausibly does, but Zac's kit carries no interruptible flag on R and needsResearch is empty, so I preserved the claim without reinforcing it.
